title: ITR for Freelancers: Forms, Methods, and Deductions Explained
description: Freelancers not requiring an audit must file their Income Tax Return (ITR) by August 31st for the previous financial year. Choosing between ITR-3 and ITR-4 de.

faq.q: Who needs to file ITR by August 31st?
faq.a: Freelancers and self-employed individuals whose accounts do not require an audit must file their ITR by August 31st for the previous financial year.

faq.q: Which ITR form should a freelancer use?
faq.a: Most freelancers will use either ITR-3 or ITR-4. ITR-4 is for those opting for presumptive taxation (gross receipts up to ₹50 lakhs), while ITR-3 is for others, including those with higher gross receipts or who declare lower profits and need to maintain detailed books.

faq.q: What is presumptive taxation under Section 44ADA?
faq.a: Section 44ADA allows eligible professionals with gross receipts up to ₹50 lakhs to declare 50% of their gross receipts as their taxable income, simplifying tax computation and exempting them from maintaining detailed books of accounts.

Yes, freelancers can claim all expenses incurred "wholly and exclusively" for their profession, such as office rent, utility bills, software subscriptions, travel, and depreciation on professional assets, if they do not opt for presumptive taxation.

faq.q: Do I need to pay advance tax as a freelancer?
faq.a: If your estimated tax liability for the financial year is ₹10,000 or more, you are required to pay advance tax in four instalments throughout the year.

faq.q: How should I report foreign income?
faq.a: Foreign income received by a Resident and Ordinarily Resident freelancer is taxable in India and must be reported under "Profits and Gains from Business or Profession," converted to INR using prescribed exchange rates.
